HASS 4개 혁신학과 통합 개편안 (8전공 → 4학과)

인문·사회·예술·정량의 통찰로 각 도메인의 혁신을 설계하는 디비전 — 8개 전공을 4개 혁신학과로 재편하는 학사구조 개편안.

학사구조 개편안·2026
CS 문화사회학과 QF 계량금융학과 DT 디자인기술학과 SG 지속거버넌스학과
1

HASS Division — 정의와 방향

통합 서사: 3학부 8전공 → 4개 혁신학과

기존 HASS는 3개 학부(아시아학부·융합사회과학부·테크노아트학부)에 8개 전공을 담은 구조였다. 이번 개편으로 8전공은 4개 혁신학과로 재편된다 — 문화사회학과(CS), 계량금융학과(QF), 디자인기술학과(DT), 지속거버넌스학과(SG). 네 학과의 명칭이 모두 '~혁신학과'로 수렴한다는 점이 디비전 전체의 정체성을 규정한다. HASS는 인문·사회·예술·정량 지식을 토대로, 각 도메인(문화·사회 / 금융 / 디자인·기술 / 지속가능성·거버넌스)의 혁신을 설계하는 디비전으로 수렴한다.

즉 HASS Division은 인문·사회·예술 전공의 행정적 집합이 아니라, 서로 다른 지식 전통이 각자의 도메인에서 혁신을 만들어내는 방식을 공유하는 혁신 디비전이다. 인문학(CS)은 문화·사회를 비판적으로 재해석하는 혁신을, 정량과학(QF)은 금융을 계량하고 갱신하는 혁신을, 디자인·기술(DT)은 제품·서비스·벤처를 창출하는 혁신을, 사회과학(SG)은 제도·정책·거버넌스를 재설계하는 사회혁신을 담당한다.

  • 미션(태그라인): 인문·사회·예술·정량의 지혜로 각 도메인의 혁신을 설계한다 — HASS, a Division of Innovation.

Division 명칭

  • 확정안(권장): HASS — Humanities, Arts & Social Sciences for Innovation. 기존 약어·브랜드 자산을 유지하면서 4개 '~혁신학과' 체제의 공통 지향(Innovation)을 부제로 명문화한다.
  • 대안: HASS Innovation Division(최소 변경) / School of Innovation Studies(혁신 전면화 신규명) / iHASS(접두 브랜딩). 세 안 모두 Innovation을 명칭에 반영하나, 기존 브랜드 연속성과 인문·예술 정체성 보존 측면에서 권장안이 우수하다.

4학과의 횡단·상호보완

네 학과는 독립적 도메인을 갖되 디비전 공통 방법론 허브로 횡단한다. QF은 통계·시계열·정량 이론의 허브(전 학과 교차수강처), SG는 계산사회과학(통계·ML·LLM)의 사회·정책 응용 허브, DT는 디자인·제작·프로토타이핑(기획→구현→사업화)의 실행 허브, CS는 문화·사회 비평(비판적 텍스트·미디어 해석)의 해석 허브다. DT의 벤처 캡스톤은 QF의 리스크 계량과 SG의 정책·거버넌스 분석을 끌어오고, CS의 문화 비평은 DT의 콘텐츠·브랜드 혁신과 SG의 문화정책 설계에 해석적 깊이를 공급한다. 혁신은 한 학과가 독점하지 않고 도메인 간 방법 이동으로 증폭된다.

Division 지도: 4학과 × 도메인 × 시그니처 방법

학과 도메인 혁신 시그니처 방법 보유 전공/트랙
CS 문화사회학과 문화·사회 혁신(비판적 재해석) 역사학·문헌 분석·문화연구(문화·미디어 비평) 아시아학 전공
QF 계량금융학과 금융 혁신(계량·핀테크) 금융 시계열·계량경제·금융공학, AI 금융 계량위험관리 전공
DT 디자인기술학과 디자인·기술 혁신(제품·서비스·벤처) 디자인 리서치·모션 데이터(HCI)·NLP·비즈니스 애널리틱스 CDM·IID·CTM 3트랙

2

진단과 통합 개요

현행 8개 전공 체제의 근본 문제는 전공 간 교과 내용의 중복이다. 216개 전 과목의 강의계획서를 임베딩해 내용 유사도를 계산하면, 행정적 전공 경계와 무관하게 특정 과목군이 서로 강하게 묶인다.

두 덩어리는 각각 디자인·기술·경영(문화디자인경영·정보인터렉션디자인·창의기술경영)과 정책·개발·법(과학기술정책·지속개발협력·사회정의리더십)이다. 특히 과학기술정책은 자기 전공 과목보다 타 전공 과목과 더 유사할 만큼 독자 정체성이 약하다. 반면 계량위험관리와 아시아학은 상대적으로 독립된 군집을 이룬다.

따라서 자연스러운 귀결은 — 뒤엉킨 두 덩어리를 각각 하나의 학과(DT 디자인기술학과, SG 지속거버넌스학과)로 통합하고, 독립적인 QF 계량금융학과·CS 문화사회학과는 단독 학과로 두는 8전공 → 4학과 개편이다.

4개 혁신학과 체제

이번 개편은 전공 축소가 아니라 HASS 전체가 각 도메인의 혁신을 추구하는 4개 혁신학과 체제로의 전환이다. 네 학과는 'Innovation'을 공통 지향으로 공유하되, 서로 다른 종류의 혁신을 담당한다.

학과(코드) 정식 학과명 어떤 혁신인가
CS 문화사회학과 (Culture & Society) 문화·사회의 혁신 — 아시아의 문화현상·미디어·사회변동을 비판적으로 읽고 재해석
QF 계량금융학과 (Quantitative Finance) 금융의 혁신 — 시계열·금융공학 코어에 핀테크·AI 금융·대체데이터·리스크 혁신
DT 디자인기술학과 (Design & Technology) 디자인·기술의 혁신 — 디자인(CDM/IID)과 기술(CTM)을 잇는 제품·서비스·벤처 혁신
SG 지속거버넌스학과 (Sustainability & Governance) 지속가능성·거버넌스의 사회혁신 — 지속가능성·정의·정책을 거버넌스와 사회혁신으로 수렴

네 학과는 "무엇을 혁신하는가"로 구별된다: 문화·사회(CS) / 금융(QF) / 디자인·기술(DT) / 지속가능성·거버넌스(SG). 코드(CS/QF/DT/SG)는 내부 식별 태그로 존치하고, 학과의 정식 명칭은 위 지향명으로 확정한다.

진단: 8전공 체제의 구조적 문제

  1. 정체성 침식: 전공 간 내용이 크게 겹치는 과목 쌍이 다수 존재했다. 특히 STP는 26과목 중 12개가 타 전공 접두사였고, JCL은 전공과목의 다수가 강사에 의존해 사실상 독립 전공의 형태를 갖추지 못했다.
  2. 운영 불안정: JCL·STP·SDC 등 소규모 전공에서 전임교원 부족, 강사 의존, 타 전공 교차개설 의존이 만성화되었다.
  3. 시대 부적합: 기후위기·AI·기술규제·ESG·불평등 같은 복합 문제는 단일 전공 지식으로 다루기 어렵고, 융합인재양성사업(HUSS) 선정은 문제해결형 융합교육의 제도화를 요구한다.

통합 원리

원리 내용
규모의 정체성 독립적으로 유지 가능한 전공(CS·QF)은 단독 학과로 존치하고, 그렇지 않은 전공은 문제·방법의 상보성으로 묶는다(DT=디자인·기술 혁신, SG=계산사회과학 기반 사회문제 해결).
한 과목, 한 소속 교차개설을 전면 해제한다. 모든 과목은 하나의 학과(및 트랙)에 귀속하고, 타 학과 학생은 교차수강으로 개방한다.
시그니처 데이터/방법론 각 학과·트랙은 고유의 데이터 유형과 방법론을 보유해, 무엇으로 무엇을 분석하는 곳인지 즉시 식별되게 한다.
폐지·신설의 절제 내용이 크게 겹치는 과목만 통합·폐지하고, 신설은 학과 정체성이 요구하나 커리큘럼에 없는 공백만 메운다.

시그니처 데이터·방법론 지도

학과/트랙 시그니처 데이터 시그니처 방법론 대표 과목(기존+신설)
CS 인문·사료 + 동시대 문화·미디어 텍스트 역사학·문헌 분석·문화연구(비판적 문화·미디어 분석) ASP3018, ASP3035, 신설 '디지털 아시아'·'아시아 문화·사회 혁신 세미나'
QF 금융 시계열 + 대체데이터 계량경제·금융공학·확률통계, AI 금융 ECO3104, QRM3003, QRM3006, 신설 '금융 시계열 분석'·'핀테크와 금융혁신'
DT‑CDM 컬처 데이터(트렌드·브랜드·전시) 문화 해석·디자인 리서치·마케팅 DSN2104, CDM2008, CDM3008
DT‑IID 모션 데이터(동작·인터랙션) HCI·UX 리서치·프로토타이핑 IID3004, IID3013, 신설 '모션 데이터 스튜디오'
DT‑CTM 비즈니스·네트워크·텍스트 NLP·비즈니스 애널리틱스 CTM2011, CTM3022, 신설 'NLP와 텍스트 애널리틱스'
SG 정책·담론·사회 데이터 계산사회과학(통계·ML·LLM) STP3013, 신설 'Applied AI Methods for Social Science'

방법론 허브의 분담: 통계·금융 이론은 QF(전 학과 교차수강처), 경영 의사결정용 애널리틱스는 DT‑CTM, 사회·정책 데이터 분석은 SG, 인문 텍스트 독해는 CS가 담당한다. 같은 텍스트 분석도 CTM은 시장·제품 인텔리전스(NLP), SG는 정책·담론 분석(LLM), CS는 사료 비판으로 목적이 다르다.

학과별 설계

CS
Culture, Society and Innovation (문화사회혁신)

문화사회학과 (Culture & Society)

아시아의 문화와 사회를 비판적으로 읽고 혁신적으로 재해석한다.
시그니처 · 인문·사료 텍스트 + 동시대 문화·미디어 텍스트 / 역사학·문헌 분석·문화연구.보유 전공 · 아시아학 전공
  • 정체성: 동아시아(한·중·일과 그 너머, 이란·이슬람권 포함)의 역사·문학·영화·사회를 1차 텍스트와 사료로 비판적으로 독해하는 인문 코어를 뿌리로 삼되, 그 독해력을 문화·사회의 혁신으로 확장하는 학과다. 지향은 아시아 인문학의 보존을 넘어, 동시대 문화현상(K-콘텐츠·팬덤·플랫폼), 미디어·알고리즘 사회, 사회변동, 문화산업·문화정책과의 접점을 비판적·해석적으로 분석하고 새롭게 의미화하는 데 있다. 견고한 인문 코어를 유지하면서 방향을 가장 크게 넓힌 학과로서, '인문 코어 + 동시대 문화·사회 혁신'의 이중 구조를 갖는다. 다만 그 혁신은 DT‑CDM(문화산업 경영)·SG(사회 정책)와 구별되는, 문화·사회를 읽고 재해석하는 인문·사회적 혁신이다.
  • 구성(29과목 체제 유지):
  • 관문: ASP1011
  • 역사: ASP2001, ASP2004, ASP2007, ASP2016, ASP2025, ASP2031, ASP2033, ASP3018
  • 문학·영화·대중문화: ASP2010, ASP2022, ASP2024, ASP2100, ASP2101, ASP3004, ASP3035, CLC3708, CLC4719, ASP2027
  • 사회·정치: ASP3007, ASP3029, ASP3031, SOC3402, SOC4305, POL3153, (유입) ISM2107 POLITICS AND BUSINESS IN KOREA — 한국 정치경제는 한국학 계보(ASP3007과 짝)
  • 법·정의의 문화사: ASP3034 OUTLAWS — 의적 서사의 문화사로 유지
  • 연구: ASP4005, ASP4009
  • 신설: 1. 디지털 아시아: 플랫폼, 팬덤, 알고리즘 사회 — 근현대에 밀집된 커리큘럼의 동시대 공백을 보완. 문화연구 방법을 유지하되 대상을 동시대 플랫폼 아시아로 확장하는 문화사회혁신 지향의 교두보. 2. 아시아 문화·사회 혁신 세미나 (Innovation in Asian Culture and Society) — 문화운동·사회변동·미디어 전환·문화정책 담론을 사례로, 아시아 사회가 문화를 통해 스스로를 재구성해 온 혁신의 계보를 비판적으로 독해·재해석하는 상급 코어. ASP3031·ASP3029·ASP3007의 동시대 확장이자 '디지털 아시아'의 이론 짝.
  • 이관: ASP3015 MEDIA ART PRODUCTION → DT‑IID. 사진·미디어아트 제작 실습은 인터랙션 탐구 영역으로, IID2016과 이론–실습 짝을 이룬다.
  • 경계: SG와는 문화·사회 혁신을 서사·역사·문화 속에서 비판적으로 읽는가(CS), 제도·정책·거버넌스로 설계하는가(SG)로 구별한다. DT‑CDM의 한국 문화·문화산업과는 문화를 경영·산업화하는가(CDM), 비판적으로 독해·재해석하는가(CS)로 구별한다. CS의 혁신은 만들고 파는 혁신이 아니라 읽고 다시 의미화하는 인문·사회적 혁신이다.
QF
Quantitative Finance and Innovation (계량금융혁신)

계량금융학과 (Quantitative Finance)

불확실성을 시계열로 계량하고, 금융의 미래를 혁신한다.
시그니처 · 금융 시계열 데이터 / 계량경제·금융공학, AI 금융·대체데이터. 커리큘럼의 정점 과목이 "시간에 따라 움직이는 위험"으로 수렴하되, 그 위험을 혁신적으로 계량·관리하는 방법(QRM3006 금융 AI 등)으로 확장한다.보유 전공 · 계량위험관리 전공
  • 정체성: 확률·통계·계량경제·금융공학으로 위험을 측정·가격화·관리하는 HASS 유일의 정량 학과이자 전교 정량·통계·금융 허브다. 정량 금융·통계 이론의 소속을 이곳으로 단일화한다. 지향은 전통적 위험관리에 머물지 않고, 그 정량 코어 위에 금융의 혁신 — 핀테크, AI 기반 금융·투자, 대체데이터, 리스크 관리 방법의 혁신 — 을 얹는 데 있다. 4학과 체제에서 QF은 (a) Finance 코어를 시계열 방법론 축으로 재정렬하고, (b) 시계열·금융공학 위에 금융혁신 트랙을 세우며, (c) DT·SG의 통계·재무 수요를 교차수강으로 수용한다.
  • 구성(24과목 + 신설 4):
  • 경제 기초: QRM1001(관문), ECO1101, ECO1103, ECO1104, ECO2101, ECO2102, QRM2001
  • 수리·통계(HASS 통계 허브): STA2102, STA2104(R·Python), STA2105, QRM3004(회귀), QRM3005(수리통계), ECO3104(계량경제 — 시계열 진입로)
  • 금융: QRM2002(금융데이터), QRM3001, QRM3002(포트폴리오), QRM3003(금융공학·파생), ECO3130(국제금융), ECO3134(화폐금융), ECO4115(기업금융), ECO4865(부동산금융)
  • AI·데이터: QRM3006(금융 AI), STA4103(데이터마이닝)
  • 가교: ECO3127(법경제학 — SG Law Certificate와의 가교)
  • 신설: 1. 금융 시계열 분석 (Financial Time Series Econometrics) — ARIMA·GARCH·변동성 모델링·고빈도 데이터. 계량 단면(ECO3104)과 파생(QRM3003) 사이의 시그니처 공백을 실체화하는 간판 과목. 시계열이 시그니처인 학과에 시계열 전담 과목이 없던 공백을 해소한다. 2. 핀테크와 금융혁신 (Fintech and Financial Innovation) — 대체데이터·AI 트레이딩·디지털 자산·리스크 혁신을 시계열·금융공학 코어 위에 얹는 상급 과목. QRM3006의 응용·산업 확장이자 계량금융혁신 지향의 간판. DT‑CTM의 디지털 비즈니스 전략(CTM3011)과는 정량 금융 모델·리스크(QF), 사업모델·경영전략(CTM)으로 구별한다. 3. 기후·재난 리스크 모델링 — 위험을 금융 밖(기후·재난·보험)으로 확장. SG의 기후 정책과는 방법(정량 모델링)으로 구별한다. 4. 베이지안 데이터 분석과 의사결정 — 수리통계(QRM3005)와 데이터마이닝(STA4103) 사이 추론 방법론 공백.
  • 폐지·통합: 자체 폐지 없음. DT‑CTM의 CTM2016(통계, QRM3004와 중복)·CTM2017(재무관리, QRM3001·ECO4115와 중복) 폐지의 흡수처가 된다. SG 2단계 통계 과목(Statistics for Social Science)은 QF 허브와 내용을 조율해 이론 중복을 방지하며, SG 쪽은 응용·해석 중심으로 운영한다.
  • 경계: DT‑CTM과는 수리 모델·통계 이론(QF), 경영 의사결정용 비즈니스 애널리틱스(CTM)로 구별한다. SG와는 금융·위험의 계량(QF), 사회·정책 데이터 분석(SG)으로 구별한다.
DT
Design, Technology and Innovation (디자인기술혁신)

디자인기술학과 (Design & Technology)

디자인(CDM·IID)과 기술(CTM)을 혁신으로 잇는다 — 문화를 해석하고, 인터랙션을 설계하고, 기술로 창업한다.
시그니처 · 컬처 데이터(트렌드·브랜드·전시·문화산업) / 문화 해석 + 디자인 경영.보유 전공 · 문화디자인경영(CDM)·정보인터렉션디자인(IID)·창의기술경영(CTM) 3트랙
  • 정체성: 3전공(CDM·IID·CTM)을 하나의 학과로 통합하되, 각 전공의 지향을 3개 트랙의 기준으로 유지한다. 학과의 지향은 디자인(CDM의 문화·제품/서비스 디자인 + IID의 인터랙션·정보 디자인)과 기술(CTM의 기술경영·IT·기업가정신)을 제품·서비스·벤처의 창출로 잇는 것이다. 통합의 목적은 트랙 융해가 아니라 (a) 공통 기초·공동 캡스톤으로 "디자인 기획(CDM)→인터랙션 구현(IID)→기술 사업화(CTM)"의 혁신 파이프라인을 한 학과 안에서 완결하게 하고, (b) 트랙 간 중복 12과목을 정리해 각 트랙의 시그니처를 선명하게 하는 것이다.
  • 학과 공통 구조:
  • 공통 관문: CDM1001·IID1001·CTM1001 중 2개 이수 권장(자기 트랙 + 인접 트랙 1) — 세 트랙의 언어를 1학년에 노출.
  • 공통 기초 툴: TAP1003(아이디어 시각화 — 舊 CDM1003 흡수 후 학과 시각화 허브), IID1008(디지털 툴), CTM1004(프로그래밍) — 트랙 무관 개방.
  • 공동 캡스톤: TAP4001 TECHNO-ART CAPSTONE(교차개설 해제, 학과 직속). CDM(제품·브랜드 기획)+IID(인터랙션 구현)+CTM(사업화) 연합팀으로 기술적 실현가능성·시장경쟁력·품질을 갖춘 신제품을 개발한다. 통합 전 3전공이 따로 수행할 수 없던 완결 구조다.
  • 신설 벤처 런치 스튜디오(CTM 주관)도 3트랙 연합팀으로 운영한다.

트랙 1: CDM — 문화와 경영 (Culture & Management)

  • 정체성: 문화·예술 산업에서 성공할 개념적·실무적 역량. ① 컬처 매니지먼트(문화예술 경영·문화 트렌드·예술·문화·마케팅 이론) ② 디자인 매니지먼트(제품/서비스 디자인·디자인 리서치·마케팅·경영). 마케팅·제품/서비스 디자인·디자인 리서치·문화산업이 CDM의 영토다.
  • 구성:
  • 공통 관문: CDM1001, CDM2007(디자인사), CDM1011
  • 컬처 매니지먼트: CDM2011, CDM3002(한국미학), CDM2001, CDM2006(문화산업), DSN2104(디자인트렌드), CDM2009(전시기획), CDM3008(예술문화 마케팅), CDM2012(문화산업 마케팅 입문으로 개편, CTM 학생의 일반 마케팅 교차수강처), CDM3009·CDM4011(브랜드 전략·미디어), CDM3010(문화와 서비스디자인), CDM4009(사회적 예술), (유입) CTM2020 CULTURE TECHNOLOGY, (유입) IID2013 공공예술
  • 디자인 매니지먼트: CDM2002→CDM2005→CDM3003→CDM3007(Design 1~4 제품 디자인 시퀀스, 프로토타이핑 CDM3003 포함), CDM3001(서비스디자인 원론), CDM2008(디자인 리서치), CDM4003(전략 마케팅 — 디자인 주도 마케팅 전략), CDM3005(디자인 프로젝트 관리), CDM4012(학제간 디자인 매니지먼트 — IID4007 수요 흡수), CDM4010(디자인 비즈니스), CDM4008(지속가능 사회혁신), DSN4116(시스템씽킹), CDM4004(산학)
  • 폐지(내부 통합): CDM3015(→CDM2012, 마케팅 입문 중복), CDM1003(→TAP1003·IID1004, 시각화 중복), CDM3014 타이포(→IID2001, 구현은 IID), CDM2010 디지털디자인(→CDM2005), CDM3012 디자인씽킹(→CDM2008), DSN3122 인터랙션디자인(→IID3004 이관 통합).
  • 신설: 글로벌 문화산업과 콘텐츠 IP 전략 — K-콘텐츠·플랫폼 유통·IP 라이선싱. 문화·예술 산업 축을 산업구조 수준에서 완성.

트랙 2: IID — HCI/인터랙션 (Human-Centered Information & Interaction)

  • 정체성: 효과적인 정보시스템 개발과 새로운 인터랙션 형식의 탐구를 인간중심 디자인 원리 위에서 수행한다. 3기둥은 정보시스템·인터랙션·인간중심 디자인(HCI/UX).
  • 구성:
  • 인간중심 디자인 기초: IID1001(관문), IID1002, IID1005, IID1006, IID1008, TAP1003, IID1004, IID2001(타이포 허브), IID2005(BRAND IN MOTION — 모션 시그니처의 조형 기초), IID3008(비주얼 시스템)
  • 정보시스템: IID2012(정보구조), IID2019(소셜 컴퓨팅), 신설 2과목(아래)
  • 인터랙션: IID3004(인터랙션디자인 — DSN3122 흡수, 아두이노 피지컬 인터랙션 포함), IID3013(UX 리서치), IID3024(휴먼-AI 인터랙션), IID3023(AI 콘텐츠), IID3025(AI 브랜드 시스템), IID3018(소셜 디지털 이노베이션), IID2016(미디어아트론) + (유입) ASP3015(미디어아트 제작 — 이론–실습 짝)
  • 비판·프로젝트: IID2100, IID2101, IID4002, IID4004(시니어 프로젝트)
  • 폐지: IID2010 디자인사(→CDM2007), IID4007(→CDM4012·TAP4001, 디자인×비즈니스는 디자인경영이므로 CDM 소관), CTM3015(→CTM 트랙, CTM3019로 통합).
  • 신설: 1. 모션 데이터 스튜디오 (Motion Data & Embodied Interaction Lab) — 동작 캡처·제스처 인식·인터랙션 로그 분석을 UX 설계에 환류. 트랙 시그니처(모션 데이터)의 실체화로, IID2005·IID3004·IID3013을 데이터 축으로 연결한다. 2. 인간중심 정보시스템 스튜디오 — 정보시스템 축의 공백 보강. 경영 IS(CTM2002)와 구별되는 인간중심 IS 설계. 3. 크리에이티브 코딩 — p5.js·제너러티브 아트·피지컬 컴퓨팅. 4. 데이터 시각화 디자인 — 정보를 경험으로 번역. IID2012 후속.
  • 트랙 간 경계: 산출물이 제품·서비스 기획이면 CDM, 인터랙티브 시스템·경험이면 IID다. 디자인사·디자인 리서치·서비스디자인은 CDM, 타이포·모션·UX·HCI 구현은 IID.

트랙 3: CTM — 기술과 창업 (Technology & Entrepreneurship)

  • 정체성: 기술경영·정보기술·기업가정신의 결합. 3역량은 ① 데이터 기반 문제 정의 ② 기술 지식의 구현 ③ 창의적 경영 전략. 기술벤처 경영 트랙이며 범용 마케팅 허브가 아니다.
  • 구성:
  • 기업가정신·전략: CTM1001(관문), CTM2010(기업가적 경영), CTM2009(투자유치), CTM2003(기술 비즈니스 전략), CTM3011(디지털 비즈니스 전략), CTM2012(기술산업 시장전략 — CDM2012와 문화/기술로 대상 분리), CTM3024(기술기업 글로벌 시장 진출 전략으로 재정의)
  • IT·기술 구현: CTM2002(정보시스템경영 — ISM2108 폐지 수요 흡수), CTM1002(IT FOUNDATION), CTM1004(프로그래밍) — STP 개설분 회수, CTM3014(스마트 서비스 시스템)
  • 데이터 분석: CTM2014(비즈니스 데이터 사이언스), CTM2011(소셜 네트워크 분석), CTM3020(네트워크 과학), CTM3022(음악정보검색 — 오디오·텍스트 정보검색), 신설 NLP 과목(아래)
  • 운영·혁신: CTM2015, CTM2018(벤처 회계), CTM3007(프로젝트 관리), CTM3025(기술기업 HRM), CTM3021(OR), CTM3013(기술혁신의 경제학), CTM3019(기술경영 도구 — CTM3015 흡수), CTM4001(지도연구)
  • 폐지: CTM2005 UX(→IID3013·CTM2003, UX는 IID 영토), CTM2016 통계(→QRM3004), CTM2017 재무관리(→QRM3001·ECO4115, 벤처 특화 내용은 CTM2009로), CTM3015(→CTM3019), CTM2020(→CDM 트랙).
  • 신설: 1. NLP와 텍스트 애널리틱스 (NLP for Business Intelligence) — 리뷰·소셜·시장 텍스트의 마이닝·감성분석·토픽모델링·LLM 응용. 트랙 시그니처(NLP)의 실체화로, CTM2014와 CTM3022 사이의 텍스트 축 공백을 채운다. SG의 Applied AI(정책·담론)와는 대상(시장·제품)으로 구별한다. 2. 벤처 런치 스튜디오 — MVP 검증→피치덱→투자 심사 실전 캡스톤. IID·CDM 연합팀. 3. AI 프로덕트 매니지먼트 — LLM 제품의 기획·수익모델·단위경제.
  • 트랙 간 경계: 마케팅은 문화·브랜드(CDM), 기술벤처 시장분석(CTM). IT는 경영 관점 IS(CTM), 인간중심 IS(IID). 데이터는 경영 애널리틱스(CTM), 통계·금융 이론(QF, 학과 밖).
SG
Sustainability, Governance and Innovation (지속가능거버넌스혁신)

지속거버넌스학과 (Sustainability & Governance)

지속가능성과 정의를 거버넌스·사회혁신으로 설계하고, 계산사회과학으로 진단한다.
시그니처 · 계산사회과학 — 통계·ML·LLM 기반 텍스트/정책 분석.보유 전공 · 통합사회과학(SG) 전공 — 舊 지속개발협력(SDC)·과학기술정책(STP)·사회정의리더십(JCL) 통합
  • 정체성: 기술전환과 지속가능성의 시대에 복합적 사회문제를 이해하고, 이를 공공성과 정의의 관점에서 해결할 수 있는 문제설계형 융합인재를 양성한다. 학과의 지향은 지속가능성·거버넌스의 사회혁신으로, 舊 SDC의 지속가능성, 舊 STP의 기술·정책 거버넌스, 舊 JCL의 규범·정의가 거버넌스와 사회혁신으로 수렴한다. AI·플랫폼·기후위기·ESG·기술규제·국제개발·사회적 불평등의 이면에 있는 사회구조와 제도적 맥락을 분석하고, 기술과 사회·법과 정책·지속가능성과 정의를 연결해 실천 가능한 대안(제도·정책·사회혁신)을 설계한다. 계산사회과학은 이 지향을 뒷받침하는 방법론 시그니처다.
  • 인재상: ① 문제를 새롭게 정의하는 인재 ② 기술과 사회를 연결하는 인재 ③ 지속가능성과 정의를 실천하는 인재 ④ 제도·정책을 설계하는 인재 ⑤ 데이터와 근거로 판단하는 인재
  • 핵심역량 4: 1. Social Diagnosis — 사회문제를 구조적으로 진단하는 능력 2. Evidence and Methods — 데이터와 방법론을 활용해 문제를 분석하는 능력 3. Governance and Design — 제도·정책·거버넌스를 설계하는 능력 4. Leadership and Practice — 현실 문제를 조정하고 실행하는 능력
  • 졸업요건: 전공 36학점 이상 / 캡스톤 1·2 전공필수(교수-학생-기관 연계 1년 프로젝트, 결과물은 논문 또는 정책보고서) / 방법론 최소 6학점 + 이론 공통 최소 6학점 이수 권장.

4단계 커리큘럼

단계 핵심역량 교육 목표
1. Foundations Social Diagnosis 통합 사회과학의 기본 문제의식 형성
2. Analytical Tools Evidence and Methods 사회문제를 분석하는 방법 습득
3. Integration Social Diagnosis + Governance and Design 미래 사회의 핵심 전환 영역 탐구
4. Practice and Application Governance and Design + Leadership and Practice 실제 문제 해결과 통합적 적용

  • 경계: QF과는 사회·정책 데이터(SG), 금융·위험 계량(QF)으로 구별한다. DT‑CTM과는 기술을 사회가 어떻게 다스리는가(SG: AI Law, STP 계열), 기업이 어떻게 경영하는가(CTM)로 구별한다. CS와는 제도·정책 분석(SG), 역사·문화 독해(CS)로 구별한다.

과목 귀속 · 신설 · 통합 효과

과목 → 학과·트랙 귀속 요약

기본 귀속 규칙

  1. 접두사 규칙: ASP/CLC/SOC/POL→CS · ECO/STA/QF→QF · CDM/IID/CTM/DSN/TAP→DT(트랙은 접두사대로) · JCL/STP/SDC/ISM/PUB→SG
  2. SG 통합과목 우선: SG 귀속 과목은 신규 통합과목 매핑이 있으면 그 과목으로 개편·흡수한다.
  3. 내용 기준 재판정: 접두사와 내용이 불일치하는 과목(교차개설 포함)은 트랙 정체성·경계 기준으로 단독 소속을 정한다.
  4. 중복 쌍 처리: 같은 소속 내 중복은 통합 폐지, 소속 간 중복은 원본 소속을 정하고 나머지를 폐지·재정의한다.

INTRODUCTION TO ASIAN STUDIES - ASP1011-01 In this gateway course to the Asian Studies major/minor, the overall aim is to introduce students to thought-provoking texts that show how power and knowledge created the worlds we inhabit in East Asia today. We begin by examining how certain assumptions we hold about time, space, and national identity came to be constructed (reimagined) in the context of 19th and 20th century imperialism in East Asia. We will consider how Euro-American modernity prompted reconceptualization of the past in linear, national time, and how (colonial) modernity both expanded and limited political and social horizons. We will conclude by reflecting on the allure and calamity of neoliberalism in contemporary East Asia, as the context within which university students today have to grapple with life-choice questions. The overall aim is to introduce students to thought-provoking texts that show how power and knowledge created the worlds we inhabit in East Asia today. Students will learn how to give presentations on academic/literary/filmic texts, presentations that are well-organized, identifying the (author's) central problematic, and offering (critical) insights based on a close reading of the text. ASP2004AS LHP_READING COLONIAL JAPAN아시아학
강의개요

AS LHP: READING COLONIAL JAPAN - ASP2004-01 This course examines Japan's modern empire from the late nineteenth century to 1945. The course readings consist of scholarly works in a number of disciplines, including anthropology, history, and literature, as well as a variety of primary sources and visual materials (cinema, photography, graphic novel, etc.) in English translation. We will look at how Japan's modern empire extended from Sakhalin Island north of the Japanese archipelago to the Solomon Islands in the South Pacific and expanded into Manchuria, areas of China, Korea, and much of Southeast Asia and Micronesia and investigate how colonial processes intrinsically demanded a political, economic, and cultural exchange through negotiation, struggle, collaboration, and resistance. Through this class, students will develop the basic skills and vocabulary to decipher the written and visual texts of Japanese history in the prewar era. At the same time, they will learn the timeline and turning points in Japanese imperial history from 1868 to 1945, focusing on such themes as settler colonialism, imperialist economy, colonial modernity, racism, To examine Japanese colonialism in Hokkaido, Okinawa, Taiwan, Korea, Manchuria, and the Nan'yo from the late 19th century to the end of World War II. ASP2007AS LHP_KOREAN WAR아시아학
강의개요

AS LHP: KOREAN WAR - ASP2007-01 Like military lookout posts along Songdo's waterfront, the irresolution of the Korean War is everywhere apparent in Korea. Official narratives about the war, in North and South Korea and elsewhere, guard their publics against dissonant memories and dangerous scholarship. As the official narrative is continually repeated, it shapes the discursive landscape and marks the horizon of loyal citizenship. In South Korea, especially among the older generation, and certainly in American public memory, the Korean War is mostly recalled as an instance of UN/American rescue that saved South Korea from communism and enabled its eventual economic ascent. In North Korea, the Korean War was a war for liberation from U.S. imperialism. The first part of the course looks at contending subjectivities that emerged during the colonial period: communists, bourgeois nationalists, fascist imperial subjects, among others. The second half of the course begins with the question, after Japan's defeat, and with US and Soviet forces occupying a partitioned Korea, what kind of governments came to power north and south of the 38th parallel? Who were targeted for exclusion or elimination? How was the war conducted? We will conclude the course by reflecting on the war's continuing impact on the two Koreas and the East Asia region. To make the Korean War more fully visible requires

ASP2010KOREAN SOCIETY AND CULTURAL REPRESENTATIONS아시아학
강의개요

KOREAN SOCIETY AND CULTURAL This course investigates Korean literature and film that embody a range of experiences of colonized Koreans in the first half of the twentieth century. The ideological propensities of literature and film that we will discuss include nativism, nationalism, socialism, modernism, and regionalism (pan-Asianism). Although the course examines "Korean" cultural representations of the modern era, the Korean nation alone fails to define the so-called Koreanness at the time. A myriad of challenges from regionalism, pan-nationalism, and globalization constituted, rather than undermined, nationalism, nurturing it as a competing ideology against non-nationalist thoughts. With this context in mind, we will study exemplary works of literature and film that epitomize paradigmatic thoughts and sentiments of the colonial era. Students will learn how to analyze given literary and cinematic texts and to make compelling arguments apropos of those texts from national, regional, and global perspectives. Built on the historical knowledge and analytical skills, course participants will also look into the recent comfort-women controversy and engage with an array of scholarly and cinematic responses to the issue. 강의개요

AS LHP: CHINESE CINEMAS; NATIONAL AND This course examines exemplary Chinese films from the Republican to contemporary periods as well as field-defining critical theories in Chinese Film Studies. As an artistic innovation, an intellectual current, and a political platform, Chinese cinema has always functioned as a site where nationalist, anti-imperial, and global identities and feelings are formed, negotiated, and remade. Key issues that we will engage throughout the semester include cinematic languages, spectatorship, modernism, left-wing criticism, ideology, national mythology, urbanism, women and the gaze, gender, class struggle, and linguistic politics and diversity. Students will gain some familiarity with films that belong to the classics of Chinese cinema; at the same time, we will learn new methods of analyzing and critiquing the linkage between " cinema" and "the nation" in the continual process of China's visual self-making in the world. 강의개요

AS LHP: MODERNITY AND CHINESE This course investigates the genesis and development of modern Chinese literature of the Republican era (1912-1949) and examines an array of canonical novels, short stories, and critical essays. We will analyze the ways that Chinese writers grappled with the task of modernization in literary and critical writing amidst various challenges and threats from Western and Japanese empires. Course participants will learn how crucial historical junctures--for instance, the 1919 May Fourth Movement, the 1927 split of United Front between the Chinese Communist and Nationalist Parties, and the Second Sino-Japanese War ( 1937-45)--shaped and reshaped literary practices of modern China. The course focuses on distinctive themes and forms of modern Chinese literature, including revolution, love, national salvation, New Woman, individual subjecthood, first-person narrative, and appropriation of an omniscient point of view. 강의개요

AS LHP: POSTWAR JAPAN: POLITICS AND What kinds of political, social, and cultural shifts accompanied Japan's surrender on August 15, 1945, when the past presumably ended and the present began? What were the competing American and Japanese visions for postwar Japan, and how did they play out during the American occupation? Keeping in our field of vision the Cold War in East Asia that involved massive American intervention in two major wars (Korea and Vietnam), this course will explore key themes and issues in the political, social, and cultural reconstitution of Japan as a nation-state following its defeat in World War II, including issues relating to the emergence (and disappearance) of a progressive intellectual community, the formation of mass culture, consumerism, and (myths of) middle class life, and certain continuities in Japan's political economy from the 1930s and the war era. To understand what cultural politics meant for postwar Japan through various forms of mass cultures, such as literature, cinema, animation (anime), manga, and art. To develop the essential skills and vocabulary to decipher Japanese mass culture's written and visual texts in the postwar era. To learn the timeline and turning points in Japanese history after 1945, focusing on such themes as war responsibility, economic growth, political movements, and consumerism. ASP2100AS LHP_STRANGER THINGS IN THE CHINESE LITERARY TRADITION아시아학
강의개요

AS LHP: STRANGER THINGS IN THE CHINESE This course examines notions about the strange, fantastic, uncanny, and grotesque through readings from Chinese antiquity to the present day. Stories that implicate these categories have traditionally explored the tenuous line between the normal and the abnormal. They have also been used to critique social norms and to articulate ideals that are unrealized in the real world. Our readings will span multiple literary genres to include foundational myths, accounts of the anomalous, stories of fox spirits and demons, Buddhist miracle tales, proto-science fiction, social satire, contemporary science fiction, and martial arts fantasy. We will discuss the ways in which the Chinese literary tradition explored how " stranger things" might be comprehended or even normalized. All readings will be in translation. Students will learn to wrestle with complex representations of the strange in the Chinese literary tradition. Students will develop close reading and critical reasoning skills through their engagement with literary texts. Students will gain a deeper understanding of how the "strange" reveals fundamental, and yet evolving, beliefs about one's world and reality, especially in the Chinese context. 40 pages per week (A4) By the end of the PBL CBL, Flipped Classroom , Close Reading Assignment ("Quiz") due Midterm Assignment due Friday, Oct 27, Tak

AS LHP: THE TRADITIONAL CHINESE NOVEL: THEN AND NOW This semester's focus will be Romance of the Three Kingdoms and Dream of the Red Chamber. All is fair in love and war. So goes the saying that reflects a widely accepted understanding that love and war may have much in common: both involve conquest and loss, sacrifices and betrayals, victors and the vanquished. This course introduces two of the greatest of the traditional Chinese novels--Romance of the Three Kingdoms and Dream of the Red Chamber--and explores some of the profound questions that underlie human conflicts in love and war through engagement with selections of celebrated chapters from these two literary masterpieces. All readings will be provided in translation. Class time will be devoted to discussing the content of the assigned chapters, and watching scenes from recent film and dramatic adaptations and comparing them with the novels. Students will analyze the literary structures, tropes, and characters in two of the four great Chinese novels and understand them in light of complex historical and cultural contexts. While South Korea is the focus of our inquiry, finding compelling answers requires historical comparisons and, for our purposes, an inter-disciplinary approach. We end by thinking about how neoliberalism shapes our life choices, and limits the horizon of possibilities. HISTORIOGRAPHY ON KOREA - ASP3018-01 (YIC) Veritas Hall B, #425 Over the past sixty years, history writing has become a varied and contentious intellectual practice. This course cannot provide a comprehensive overview of the academic discipline of history, nor a comprehensive overview of historiography on Korea. Instead, it introduces a set of topics, problematics, and theoretical concerns in history writing that can be seen as "critical" to historical knowledge today especially for South Koreans. The topics/problematics we will address include: colonialism and de-colonization in comparative perspective; and "new" approaches/problematics in scholarship on North and South Korea. We will end the course with examination of history education in China, Japan, and Korea, and the politics of "history wars." Deep knowledge of Korean history is not a prerequisite. Students will become familiar with select topics, problematics, and theoretical concerns that are central to gaining deep historical knowledge about modern Korea. GENDER AND KOREAN SOCIETY - ASP3029-01 (YIC) Veritas Hall B, # 425 In this course we will look at how Korean society has been (re-)imagined and (re-)organized in gendered ways. Starting from the pre-modern period and moving to the present, we will examine the nexus between structures of power and the production of gendered identities and practices. Our field of vision will be both local and global as we examine the intersection of gender, sexuality, race, and class in situations of dynastic formation, colonialism, war mobilization, capitalist industrialization, and neoliberal restructuring of not just the economy, but also desire, affect, and personhood. We will end by reflecting on the possibilities for equality, justice, and connection. By way of comparisons with ancient Greece, students will gain both insight and perspective on the position of women in Choson Korea, from the kwan'gi (government courtesans) to yangban women and With the onset of colonialism and modernity, students will gain insight into new articulations of masculinity and femininity, including the call for revolutionary feminism on the one hand, and the Wise Mother, Good Wife on the other. With war mobilization toward the end of the colonial period, followed by the (unending) Korean War, students will gain insight into how militarism continues to shape gendered identities and practices in South Korea. DEMOCRACY IN SOUTH KOREA - ASP3031-01 Today, no one would deny that democracy has taken root in South Korea. How do we draw the line between lawful and unlawful, just and unjust? Is a "righteous outlaw" a contradiction in terms? This course explores traditional narratives of law and justice that have influenced Chinese, Japanese, and Korean cultures by focusing on figures that challenge law and order. These figures raise questions such as: how do we achieve justice within and beyond legal institutions, how do we deal with injustices imposed by the law or by legal actors, and what happens when the bad guys become good? By analyzing literary texts about those who transgress the law, we explore how notions of justice have been variously conceived and problematized in East Asian cultures. All readings will be in Students will learn to wrestle with complex representations of crime and justice in the East Asian traditions. Students will develop close reading and critical reasoning skills through their engagement with literary texts. Students will gain a deeper understanding of contemporary East Asian legal cultures and how they are influenced by traditional attitudes toward crime and justice. 40 pages per week (A4) By the end of the PBL CBL, Flipped Classroom , Close Reading Assignment due Midterm Assignment due Friday, Oct 27, Timely and regular attendance is required, as well as active participation. POLITICS AND BUSINESS IN KOREA - ISM2107-01 This course aims to examine the Korean politics and business from the political economy perspective. How Korean capitalism has developed, what pathway it has taken and how it will continue to evolve, and how politics and business have interacted in Korean capitalist market are the puzzles of this course. This course will cover the various topics in the environment of business (market and non-market environments ) such as globalization, democratization, culture and network, international investment and trade, Asian crisis in 1997, global crash in 2008, economic reform, types of recovery or recession, public and private governance, global pandemic and the current political economic debates (fairness and justice issues in Korea). In particular, we will reassess and recast the politics-business relationship through further case studies of Korean large conglomerates (Chaebol) and related salient economic institutions. The main focus throughout this course will be on the roles and interests of government, business, civil society, and foreign investor. Students are expected to cultivate and apply their own point of views and conceptual frameworks regarding Korean politics and business. The term resiliency, used to describe the robust fitness of Chinese authoritarianism, refers to the capacity of open systems to reorganize itself in order to maintain its basic structure and function. Such a dynamic conception of resiliency defies the perception of the Chinese party-state as a stagnant system on the brink of decline or at a breaking point. This course will examine the tangible components, social contexts, and subtexts that have shaped and continue to shape the Chinese Communist Party's (CCP) adaptive behavior to confer resilience to change and challenges. Upon completion of the course, you should be able to: Comprehend the idiosyncrasies of the CCP's operational milieu, including the ordering principle and the functional differentiation of self-similar units, which enable the system to cope with stresses and Gain a base of concepts and skills needed to understand the process of politicization within Chinese legislative, consultative, legal, military, and educational institutions. AS LHP: READING COLONIAL JAPAN - ASP2004-01 This course examines Japan's modern empire from the late nineteenth century to 1945. The course readings consist of scholarly works in a number of disciplines, including anthropology, history, and literature, as well as a variety of primary sources and visual materials (cinema, photography, graphic novel, etc.) in English translation. We will look at how Japan's modern empire extended from Sakhalin Island north of the Japanese archipelago to the Solomon Islands in the South Pacific and expanded into Manchuria, areas of China, Korea, and much of Southeast Asia and Micronesia and investigate how colonial processes intrinsically demanded a political, economic, and cultural exchange through negotiation, struggle, collaboration, and resistance. Through this class, students will develop the basic skills and vocabulary to decipher the written and visual texts of Japanese history in the prewar era. At the same time, they will learn the timeline and turning points in Japanese imperial history from 1868 to 1945, focusing on such themes as settler colonialism, imperialist economy, colonial modernity, racism, To examine Japanese colonialism in Hokkaido, Okinawa, Taiwan, Korea, Manchuria, and the Nan'yo from the late 19th century to the end of World War II. ASP2007AS LHP_KOREAN WAR아시아·문화유지
강의개요

AS LHP: KOREAN WAR - ASP2007-01 Like military lookout posts along Songdo's waterfront, the irresolution of the Korean War is everywhere apparent in Korea. Official narratives about the war, in North and South Korea and elsewhere, guard their publics against dissonant memories and dangerous scholarship. As the official narrative is continually repeated, it shapes the discursive landscape and marks the horizon of loyal citizenship. In South Korea, especially among the older generation, and certainly in American public memory, the Korean War is mostly recalled as an instance of UN/American rescue that saved South Korea from communism and enabled its eventual economic ascent. In North Korea, the Korean War was a war for liberation from U.S. imperialism. The first part of the course looks at contending subjectivities that emerged during the colonial period: communists, bourgeois nationalists, fascist imperial subjects, among others. The second half of the course begins with the question, after Japan's defeat, and with US and Soviet forces occupying a partitioned Korea, what kind of governments came to power north and south of the 38th parallel? Who were targeted for exclusion or elimination? How was the war conducted? We will conclude the course by reflecting on the war's continuing impact on the two Koreas and the East Asia region. KOREAN SOCIETY AND CULTURAL This course investigates Korean literature and film that embody a range of experiences of colonized Koreans in the first half of the twentieth century. The ideological propensities of literature and film that we will discuss include nativism, nationalism, socialism, modernism, and regionalism (pan-Asianism). Although the course examines "Korean" cultural representations of the modern era, the Korean nation alone fails to define the so-called Koreanness at the time. A myriad of challenges from regionalism, pan-nationalism, and globalization constituted, rather than undermined, nationalism, nurturing it as a competing ideology against non-nationalist thoughts. With this context in mind, we will study exemplary works of literature and film that epitomize paradigmatic thoughts and sentiments of the colonial era. Students will learn how to analyze given literary and cinematic texts and to make compelling arguments apropos of those texts from national, regional, and global perspectives. Built on the historical knowledge and analytical skills, course participants will also look into the recent comfort-women controversy and engage with an array of scholarly and cinematic responses to the issue. 강의개요

AS LHP: MODERNITY AND CHINESE This course investigates the genesis and development of modern Chinese literature of the Republican era (1912-1949) and examines an array of canonical novels, short stories, and critical essays. We will analyze the ways that Chinese writers grappled with the task of modernization in literary and critical writing amidst various challenges and threats from Western and Japanese empires. Course participants will learn how crucial historical junctures--for instance, the 1919 May Fourth Movement, the 1927 split of United Front between the Chinese Communist and Nationalist Parties, and the Second Sino-Japanese War ( 1937-45)--shaped and reshaped literary practices of modern China. The course focuses on distinctive themes and forms of modern Chinese literature, including revolution, love, national salvation, New Woman, individual subjecthood, first-person narrative, and appropriation of an omniscient point of view. ASP2025AS LHP_POSTWAR JAPAN_POLITICS AND CULTURE아시아·문화유지
강의개요

AS LHP: POSTWAR JAPAN: POLITICS AND What kinds of political, social, and cultural shifts accompanied Japan's surrender on August 15, 1945, when the past presumably ended and the present began? What were the competing American and Japanese visions for postwar Japan, and how did they play out during the American occupation? Keeping in our field of vision the Cold War in East Asia that involved massive American intervention in two major wars (Korea and Vietnam), this course will explore key themes and issues in the political, social, and cultural reconstitution of Japan as a nation-state following its defeat in World War II, including issues relating to the emergence (and disappearance) of a progressive intellectual community, the formation of mass culture, consumerism, and (myths of) middle class life, and certain continuities in Japan's political economy from the 1930s and the war era. To understand what cultural politics meant for postwar Japan through various forms of mass cultures, such as literature, cinema, animation (anime), manga, and art. To develop the essential skills and vocabulary to decipher Japanese mass culture's written and visual texts in the postwar era. To learn the timeline and turning points in Japanese history after 1945, focusing on such themes as war responsibility, economic growth, political movements, and consumerism. For the latter half of the semester, we will analyze cultural works of our own time, ranging from literature, graphic novel (comic strip), film, and TV series, which are replete with poignant and eye-opening accounts of human experiences at the marginalized corners of the world. Toward the end of the semester, we will be able to revise existing studies on globalization and also decenter first-world-oriented views of the global. NORTH KOREA: HISTORY, CULTURE, POLITICS - ASP2033-01 As introduction to the course, we begin with an examination of how North Korea becomes legible and visible to us. What seems like propaganda, what seems like the "real" North Korea, and why? From there, we will examine North Korea's revolutionary origins (1920s-1950), with impressive strides made, prior to the Korean War, at overcoming class and gender oppression. Following the Korean War, however, we will look at how class and gender were emptied of their radical potential in the 1950s and Moving to more contemporary times, we will take a critical look at extremely politicized questions like defector testimonies and human rights, regime type and famine in the late 1990s, and North Korea's nuclear weapons program in the context of an unending Korean War. After more than 70 years of intense hostility, it is an understatement to say that disrespect is deeply entrenched on all sides. Respect is derived from the Latin re-specere, to look back at, to look again. A central aim of this course is to look back, and look again, at both North Korea and ourselves. Students will learn how to give presentations on academic/literary/filmic texts, presentations that are well-organized, identifying the (author's) central problematic, and offering (critical) insights based on a close reading of the text. ASP2100AS LHP_STRANGER THINGS IN THE CHINESE LITERARY TRADITION아시아·문화유지
강의개요

AS LHP: STRANGER THINGS IN THE CHINESE This course examines notions about the strange, fantastic, uncanny, and grotesque through readings from Chinese antiquity to the present day. Stories that implicate these categories have traditionally explored the tenuous line between the normal and the abnormal. They have also been used to critique social norms and to articulate ideals that are unrealized in the real world. Our readings will span multiple literary genres to include foundational myths, accounts of the anomalous, stories of fox spirits and demons, Buddhist miracle tales, proto-science fiction, social satire, contemporary science fiction, and martial arts fantasy. We will discuss the ways in which the Chinese literary tradition explored how " stranger things" might be comprehended or even normalized. All readings will be in translation. Students will learn to wrestle with complex representations of the strange in the Chinese literary tradition. Students will develop close reading and critical reasoning skills through their engagement with literary texts. Students will gain a deeper understanding of how the "strange" reveals fundamental, and yet evolving, beliefs about one's world and reality, especially in the Chinese context. 40 pages per week (A4) By the end of the PBL CBL, Flipped Classroom , Close Reading Assignment ("Quiz") due Midterm Assignment due Friday, Oct 27, Tak

AS LHP: THE TRADITIONAL CHINESE NOVEL: THEN AND NOW This semester's focus will be Romance of the Three Kingdoms and Dream of the Red Chamber. All is fair in love and war. So goes the saying that reflects a widely accepted understanding that love and war may have much in common: both involve conquest and loss, sacrifices and betrayals, victors and the vanquished. This course introduces two of the greatest of the traditional Chinese novels--Romance of the Three Kingdoms and Dream of the Red Chamber--and explores some of the profound questions that underlie human conflicts in love and war through engagement with selections of celebrated chapters from these two literary masterpieces. All readings will be provided in translation. Class time will be devoted to discussing the content of the assigned chapters, and watching scenes from recent film and dramatic adaptations and comparing them with the novels. Students will analyze the literary structures, tropes, and characters in two of the four great Chinese novels and understand them in light of complex historical and cultural contexts. AS LHP: CAPITALISM AND ITS CRITICS; KOREA (YIC) Veritas Hall B #425 Ms. Junha CHO <jcho@ Capitalism need not produce massive inequalities. But today, in almost all capitalist economies, we see staggering levels of inequality in wealth and income. How and why does this happen? How are inequalities created and reproduced? What are the consequences of rising inequality and reduced intergenerational income mobility for sense of community, solidarity, and democracy? While South Korea is the focus of our inquiry, finding compelling answers requires historical comparisons and, for our purposes, an inter-disciplinary approach. This includes reading texts that bring into view race, gender, and class in specific historical contexts, such as Heartland: A Memoir of Working Hard and Being Broke in the Richest When we focus on Korea, our inquiry begins with how land and labor came to be thoroughly commodified, and how Korean day-laborers and Korean capitalists functioned in the Japanese After the Korean War, we will look closely at South Korea's history of developmentalism and neo-liberalism, and think about why we must also consider shifts in the post-WW II history of American empire. We end by thinking about how neoliberalism shapes our life choices, and limits the horizon of possibilities. HISTORIOGRAPHY ON KOREA - ASP3018-01 (YIC) Veritas Hall B, #425 Over the past sixty years, history writing has become a varied and contentious intellectual practice. This course cannot provide a comprehensive overview of the academic discipline of history, nor a comprehensive overview of historiography on Korea. Instead, it introduces a set of topics, problematics, and theoretical concerns in history writing that can be seen as "critical" to historical knowledge today especially for South Koreans. The topics/problematics we will address include: colonialism and de-colonization in comparative perspective; and "new" approaches/problematics in scholarship on North and South Korea. We will end the course with examination of history education in China, Japan, and Korea, and the politics of "history wars." Deep knowledge of Korean history is not a prerequisite. Students will become familiar with select topics, problematics, and theoretical concerns that are central to gaining deep historical knowledge about modern Korea. ASP3029GENDER AND KOREAN SOCIETY아시아·문화유지
강의개요

GENDER AND KOREAN SOCIETY - ASP3029-01 (YIC) Veritas Hall B, # 425 In this course we will look at how Korean society has been (re-)imagined and (re-)organized in gendered ways. Starting from the pre-modern period and moving to the present, we will examine the nexus between structures of power and the production of gendered identities and practices. Our field of vision will be both local and global as we examine the intersection of gender, sexuality, race, and class in situations of dynastic formation, colonialism, war mobilization, capitalist industrialization, and neoliberal restructuring of not just the economy, but also desire, affect, and personhood. We will end by reflecting on the possibilities for equality, justice, and connection. By way of comparisons with ancient Greece, students will gain both insight and perspective on the position of women in Choson Korea, from the kwan'gi (government courtesans) to yangban women and With the onset of colonialism and modernity, students will gain insight into new articulations of masculinity and femininity, including the call for revolutionary feminism on the one hand, and the Wise Mother, Good Wife on the other. With war mobilization toward the end of the colonial period, followed by the (unending) Korean War, students will gain insight into how militarism continues to shape gendered identities and practices in South Korea. DEMOCRACY IN SOUTH KOREA - ASP3031-01 Today, no one would deny that democracy has taken root in South Korea. But just how democratic is South Korea today at home, at work, in terms of relationships, and in the public square? In the first half of the course, we examine historical/theoretical questions like Who invented human rights? Can we construct an ethics solely based on human history? In the second half of the course, we consider new ways of narrating the history of the democratic movement, and identify and rethink both "old" and new A central aim of this course is to have students rethink their assumptions about "democracy." Ultimately, students should be able to see how the conception and practice of democracy itself is part of a truth process grounded in history. ASP3034OUTLAWS아시아·문화유지
강의개요

How do we draw the line between lawful and unlawful, just and unjust? Is a "righteous outlaw" a contradiction in terms? This course explores traditional narratives of law and justice that have influenced Chinese, Japanese, and Korean cultures by focusing on figures that challenge law and order. These figures raise questions such as: how do we achieve justice within and beyond legal institutions, how do we deal with injustices imposed by the law or by legal actors, and what happens when the bad guys become good? By analyzing literary texts about those who transgress the law, we explore how notions of justice have been variously conceived and problematized in East Asian cultures. All readings will be in Students will learn to wrestle with complex representations of crime and justice in the East Asian traditions. Students will develop close reading and critical reasoning skills through their engagement with literary texts. Students will gain a deeper understanding of contemporary East Asian legal cultures and how they are influenced by traditional attitudes toward crime and justice. 40 pages per week (A4) By the end of the PBL CBL, Flipped Classroom , Close Reading Assignment due Midterm Assignment due Friday, Oct 27, Timely and regular attendance is required, as well as active participation. POLITICS AND BUSINESS IN KOREA - ISM2107-01 This course aims to examine the Korean politics and business from the political economy perspective. How Korean capitalism has developed, what pathway it has taken and how it will continue to evolve, and how politics and business have interacted in Korean capitalist market are the puzzles of this course. This course will cover the various topics in the environment of business (market and non-market environments ) such as globalization, democratization, culture and network, international investment and trade, Asian crisis in 1997, global crash in 2008, economic reform, types of recovery or recession, public and private governance, global pandemic and the current political economic debates (fairness and justice issues in Korea). In particular, we will reassess and recast the politics-business relationship through further case studies of Korean large conglomerates (Chaebol) and related salient economic institutions. The main focus throughout this course will be on the roles and interests of government, business, civil society, and foreign investor. Students are expected to cultivate and apply their own point of views and conceptual frameworks regarding Korean politics and business. 강의개요

The term resiliency, used to describe the robust fitness of Chinese authoritarianism, refers to the capacity of open systems to reorganize itself in order to maintain its basic structure and function. Such a dynamic conception of resiliency defies the perception of the Chinese party-state as a stagnant system on the brink of decline or at a breaking point. This course will examine the tangible components, social contexts, and subtexts that have shaped and continue to shape the Chinese Communist Party's (CCP) adaptive behavior to confer resilience to change and challenges. Upon completion of the course, you should be able to: Comprehend the idiosyncrasies of the CCP's operational milieu, including the ordering principle and the functional differentiation of self-similar units, which enable the system to cope with stresses and Gain a base of concepts and skills needed to understand the process of politicization within Chinese legislative, consultative, legal, military, and educational institutions. widang 425 Thursday 4-5pm, Friday 3-4pm This undergraduate course provides a comparative and theoretical introduction to the recent social transformation of East Asian societies. In the first half, we will study the reform and opening up of "Actually Existing Socialism" in China. For this, we will read the theories of Marx and Lenin to make sense of issues in post-socialist transformation. Socialism in theory by Marx and Lenin used to be an alternative vision to western, liberal capitalism to some countries, but socialism in reality has been disasterous and almost disappeared on earth. The topics of working class politics, human rights and democracy, resistance and struggle from below, and globalization will be In the second half, we will move to the topics of gender and citizenship. For this, we will read a few articles by contemporary feminists, then examine the contemporary issues faced by women and minority in East Asia. In this part, we will collectively examine and grapple with the problem of social exclusion and discrimination in East Asia today. For this part you will have a chance to present your final paper with other members of your group. You will have experiences of "learning by doing" in this half. PRINCIPLES OF MACROECONOMICS is an introductory course in macroeconomics. In this course, broadly speaking we will deal with three issues: Firstly, we will think about the issue of what "wealth" is! 강의개요

The goal of this course is in introducing popular skills for analyzing economic data. We attempt to achieve this goal by getting familiar with the well-known econometric analyses and linking this to the knowledge about the numerical outputs generated by standard statistical packages. In attaining this goal, our interests will be focused more on cross-sectional data and their slight extensions. There are two reasons for this focus. First, the analysis of cross-sectional data is a building block for the analysis of many other data sets. Second, the analysis of cross-sectional data is easier than analyzing other data sets as they do not involve too much complication that comes from the variation assumptions. Eventually, by these, studying cross-sectional data becomes a good starting point for achieving the specified objectives, even though their applicability is not so limited. After completing this course, average students are expected to be able to conduct the following: o Understanding the implicit assumptions behind economic data analysis; o Interpreting the numerical outputs generated by standard statistical packages. PRINCIPLES OF MACROECONOMICS is an introductory course in macroeconomics. In this course, broadly speaking we will deal with three issues: Firstly, we will think about the issue of what "wealth" is! To begin with, we will study how a nation`s income is measured. Then, we will discuss the limits/defects of the standard way to identify wealth. Secondly, we will study the issue of the growth of wealth: how some countries have successfully achieved prosperity, while other countries have failed in achieving economic growth will be our concern to discuss in the class Thirdly, we will study theories of business cycle, the main topic of macroeconomics since John Maynard Keynes. To begin with, we will think about the very nature of money and the way financial system has been working. Also we will discuss the problem of lack of jobs available in this economy. Then, we will learn various economic theories from opposing schools that aim to smooth out economic Overall we will think about the better world economy through this course. ECO3104계량경제학(1)금융·계량유지
강의개요

The goal of this course is in introducing popular skills for analyzing economic data. We attempt to achieve this goal by getting familiar with the well-known econometric analyses and linking this to the knowledge about the numerical outputs generated by standard statistical packages. In attaining this goal, our interests will be focused more on cross-sectional data and their slight extensions. There are two reasons for this focus. First, the analysis of cross-sectional data is a building block for the analysis of many other data sets. Second, the analysis of cross-sectional data is easier than analyzing other data sets as they do not involve too much complication that comes from the variation assumptions. Eventually, by these, studying cross-sectional data becomes a good starting point for achieving the specified objectives, even though their applicability is not so limited. After completing this course, average students are expected to be able to conduct the following: o Understanding the implicit assumptions behind economic data analysis; o Interpreting the numerical outputs generated by standard statistical packages. ASP3015MEDIA ART PRODUCTION아시아학
강의개요

MEDIA ART PRODUCTION - ASP3015-01 This is a seminar course with a significant production/lab component that explores the medium of photography. It brings together readings in the Euro-American tradition of photographic theory and considers it alongside and against the grain of the Asian context. Instead of superimposing theory from one side unto the other, we consider the development and experience of photography in various locations across Asia to explore how the two might be read together. The practice component approaches writing and photography as interrelated practices of thought and being in the world. Whether we are reading about photography, looking at photographs, or making photographs of our own, the broader impulse is to link together reading, writing, listening, seeing, feeling and photographing as interrelated experiences. To do this, we will write and photograph frequently. We will do freewriting exercises together in class, as a group and also individually, employing writing and photo-graphy as a mode of thinking and being present to the emergent. We will read our writing aloud to one another. We will attend to one another's photos. We will "listen compositionally," as the anthropologist Kathleen Stewart suggests. Each piece of writing and photo-graphy will be an experiment because we don't know beforehand what the outcome will be. Peter Elbow, the composition sc

DESIGN & CITY IN CULTURE - CDM1011-01 The target audience: undergraduate students in CRS dept in CUHK and in HASS dept in Yonsei University This course will build on skills and knowledge learned through the foundation years. Students will use design thinking process, city related imagery as modes of visual communication and cultural studies. We will focus on these objectives: 1) Develop conceptual and formal communication systems with a focus on the use of visual elements and cultural studies. You will learn to create considered relationships among and between each part within the context of the whole. 2) Develop the ability to parse complexity in order to create an understanding of culture, designing within human contexts. 3) Continue to develop the technical skills relevant to producing professional-quality comps across a variety of formats building on work from Design Thinking. Additionally, we will investigate how effectively design and city relied intrinsically on its cultural environment. A question that commonly arises is how to visually communicate information between different cultures. Through some city environment projects students will demystify, depoliticize, and reconcile multiple cultures to improve communication and cultural representation. We will transcend the cultural borders using a design language. ** Selected 10 students will get a chance to visit Hong Kon

CDM2001CULTURE AND DESIGN TRENDS문화디자인경영
강의개요

CULTURE AND DESIGN TRENDS - CDM2001-01 This class is designed to extend the participants' concept of the image. Because we are, nowdays, living in the massive wave of images, it gets more important to read and edit your personalized point of view especially, for those who are specialized in image making. Its also essential for us to developing and utilizing the images in the direction of the medium that they've chosen. We also focus on reading and manipulating images with the 'personal gaze' that we are missing in the "era of image surplus". The discovery of "your personal grain" you already have is essential to reading and editing the images. This is because the perspective of the viewer's life through the same image can give a new context to the image. Through various directional workshops, This class tries to induce the discovery of the gaze projected by each one's life and to train the images into their own story. The first project for this training is a reinterpretation of Rake's Progress, a classic storytelling illustration. William Hogarth's Rake's Progress tells a person's life with eight images. Beginning with the background of the protagonist and the sudden changes in his environment, this series of pictures shows the choices he makes and the consequences. CONTEMPORARY TOPICS IN CULTURAL Our world is changing very rapidly. The digital and the physical world are converging, and technology is increasingly being embedded into our daily lives. AI is replacing our jobs, and big data collected by pervasive sensors self-adjust our smart environments to improve user experiences. Then, how will these changes affect our culture and the design industry? In this course, we delve into two crucial themes that greatly impact our cultural industry: Open Innovation and Digital-Physical Convergence. You do not need any course prerequisites to take the class; only sincerity and a willingness to innovate our life. Upon completion of this course, students will acquire in-depth knowledge of the latest trends and issues in the cultural industry. Students will also practice strong critical thinking skills by completing two mini-projects projects aimed at generating innovative ideas for cultural businesses. The students will be able to comprehend the connections between culture, technologies, and our lifestyles, especially in the 4th industrial revolution era. HISTORY OF MODERN AND CONTEMPORARY The course explores the evolution of design in order to build up the comprehensive reference for future practice in the related field. It will follow the changes of time in cultural, social, political, economic and technical terms at large and discover how those changes influenced the movements and styles in detail that eventually changed everyday life. The course will be led to an open conclusion of defining the ` contemporary' that we are living in now, on the foundation of the historical understanding of design. The course will provide series of lectures and following discussions. Lectures will offer a chronological overview on history of modern and contemporary design through the movements, styles, key designers and objects. In the following discussions, the innovations, methodologies and definitions that are conceived by design in stages will be debated, followed by student's presentations of their in-depth researches on some selected designers. *Midterm exam will be replaced by individual assignment. *Final exam will be replaced by individual submission. CTM3011DIGITAL BUSINESS STRATEGY창의기술경영
강의개요

DIGITAL BUSINESS STRATEGY - CTM3011-01 This is an advanced undergraduate course on the digital economy and the digital business strategy. Three main goals are (1) to understand how people and companies interact in the digital markets, (2) to understand how digital markets should be designed and regulated and (3) to understand how managers can formulate and execute business strategies by leveraging digital resources to create differential value. The course uses a combination of theoretical modeling and empirical evidence in order to achieve these goals. We analyze some key features that are prevalent in digital markets, including network effects, two-sided markets, search and matching, reputation systems and the use of data. We also look into individual markets such as search engines, e-commerce platforms, and media. To understand how people and companies interact in the digital economy. We study how digital technology changes economic activities. We look into the reduction in five distinct economic costs associated with digital economic activity: search costs, replication costs, transportation costs, tracking costs, and verification costs. We also learn about the digital economy eco-system and digital market To study the scope and extent of digital business strategy. We learn about organizational strategy formulated and executed by leveraging digital resources to create differe

CTM3013ECONOMICS OF TECHNOLOGICAL INNOVATION창의기술경영
강의개요

This course is designed to provide a working knowledge of economic principles and real world practices on a range of topics pertaining to technology and innovation. After the brief overview of fundamentals of economics, we will cover various topics including (1) dynamic process of innovation and corporate strategy such as disruptive innovation, vertical integration vs. modularization, learning curve, and determinants of R&D intensity; (2) success and failure of innovative activities; (3) utilization issues of innovation output including first-mover advantage, battles for winner-take-all, patents and standards. The course introduces students to basic economic principles and theories on a range of topics relevant to technology and innovation. The course helps students learn how to apply relevant concepts and frameworks in practice through real-world case studies. 강의개요

MUSIC INFORMATION RETRIEVAL - CTM3022-01 Music information retrieval (MIR) is an emerging field of research that aims to provide intelligent solutions for music listening, performance and other musical activities. This course will introduce various topics in MIR research, and explores how different types of music information can be applied to music discovery, music analysis, interactive performance, visualization, and more. In particular, we will focus on music analysis applying the approach of natural language processing .The goal of this class is to overview the topics and tasks in the field of MIR, and to conduct their own academic research. Introduction to MIR Topics: The course aims to provide an overview of various topics in MIR research. Students will be introduced to the fundamental concepts, techniques, and methodologies employed in the field. This includes understanding the different types of music information, such as audio, symbolic, and textual data, and how they can be extracted and analyzed using computational approaches. The course emphasizes the practical application of music information in various domains. Students will learn how MIR techniques can be utilized for music analysis and visualization. Academic Research: The course aims to develop students' skills and knowledge to independently conduct academic research in MIR. They will explore existing literature

강의개요

INTERNATIONAL MARKETING - CTM3024-01 The course aims to familiarize students with essential marketing concepts and practices in the global business environment. Additionally, it aims to provide students with the basic knowledge, techniques, and practical skills necessary to analyze the global marketing environment, formulate and execute an international marketing strategy, and coordinate marketing programs in the international marketplace. A particular emphasis will be placed on the concepts of standardization versus adaptation in the context of global marketing strategies. Upon completion of this course, students will be able to: 1. Evaluate the international marketing environment, specifically examining how global market dynamics and trends influence the selection of country markets and the creation of global marketing campaigns. 2. Compare and contrast various foreign market entry strategies. 3. Utilize marketing concepts to develop global marketing strategies and critically assess key factors for their successful implementation. IID2010DESIGN HISTORY폐지
강의개요

DESIGN HISTORY - IID2010-01 his introductory course is open to all students interested in art and design. It explores the intertwined histories of these fields, from 40,000-year-old cave paintings to contemporary art, emphasizing their shared roots and unique paths. In early human history, art and design were inseparable, both serving functional purposes. The Renaissance marked a shift, elevating artists and birthing fine art, while the Industrial Revolution brought design into its own through mass production. Despite their divergence, art and design remain deeply connected, using the same visual language and influencing each other. Through lectures and hands-on activities like discussions, museum visits, and team projects, this course offers a comprehensive overview of design history and its relationship with art. Join us to uncover the creative forces that shape both disciplines. Explore the Interconnected Histories of Art and Design Understand the shared origins of art and design, tracing their evolution from early functional creations to their modern and distinct roles, while recognizing their ongoing interdependence. Analyze Key Historical Turning Points Examine pivotal moments in history, such as the Renaissance and the Industrial Revolution, that shaped the divergence of art and design, and consider their impact on contemporary practices. Engage in Critical and Practical

To ensure a thorough understanding and application of concepts, students will engage in lab exercises in Python, contribute to discussions on provided topics and readings, and collaborate on a group-based final project. TECHNO-ART CAPSTONE PROJECT - TAP4001-01 The goal of this course is to develop product or service prototypes of innovative ideas. Each team should generate a new product that has technical feasibility, market competitiveness, and quality design. The teams of 4-5 students will go through 4 stages of product design and development process: discover, define, develop, and deliver. The instructors and a pool of industrial coaches will guide the progress and teams will make a classroom presentation periodically during the semester. DESIGN & CITY IN CULTURE - CDM1011-01 The target audience: undergraduate students in CRS dept in CUHK and in HASS dept in Yonsei University This course will build on skills and knowledge learned through the foundation years. Students will use design thinking process, city related imagery as modes of visual communication and cultural studies. We will focus on these objectives: 1) Develop conceptual and formal communication systems with a focus on the use of visual elements and cultural studies. You will learn to create considered relationships among and between each part within the context of the whole. 2) Develop the ability to parse complexity in order to create an understanding of culture, designing within human contexts. 3) Continue to develop the technical skills relevant to producing professional-quality comps across a variety of formats building on work from Design Thinking. Additionally, we will investigate how effectively design and city relied intrinsically on its cultural environment. A question that commonly arises is how to visually communicate information between different cultures. Through some city environment projects students will demystify, depoliticize, and reconcile multiple cultures to improve communication and cultural representation. We will transcend the cultural borders using a design language. ** Selected 10 students will get a chance to visit Hong Kon

CDM2001CULTURE AND DESIGN TRENDSCDM유지
강의개요

CULTURE AND DESIGN TRENDS - CDM2001-01 This class is designed to extend the participants' concept of the image. Because we are, nowdays, living in the massive wave of images, it gets more important to read and edit your personalized point of view especially, for those who are specialized in image making. Its also essential for us to developing and utilizing the images in the direction of the medium that they've chosen. We also focus on reading and manipulating images with the 'personal gaze' that we are missing in the "era of image surplus". The discovery of "your personal grain" you already have is essential to reading and editing the images. This is because the perspective of the viewer's life through the same image can give a new context to the image. Through various directional workshops, This class tries to induce the discovery of the gaze projected by each one's life and to train the images into their own story. The first project for this training is a reinterpretation of Rake's Progress, a classic storytelling illustration. William Hogarth's Rake's Progress tells a person's life with eight images. Beginning with the background of the protagonist and the sudden changes in his environment, this series of pictures shows the choices he makes and the consequences. This work presented people at that time with new possibilities for ' storytelling with images'. In this class, we

CDM2006CONTEMPORARY TOPICS IN CULTURAL INDUSTRYCDM유지
강의개요

CONTEMPORARY TOPICS IN CULTURAL Our world is changing very rapidly. The digital and the physical world are converging, and technology is increasingly being embedded into our daily lives. AI is replacing our jobs, and big data collected by pervasive sensors self-adjust our smart environments to improve user experiences. Then, how will these changes affect our culture and the design industry? In this course, we delve into two crucial themes that greatly impact our cultural industry: Open Innovation and Digital-Physical Convergence. You do not need any course prerequisites to take the class; only sincerity and a willingness to innovate our life. Upon completion of this course, students will acquire in-depth knowledge of the latest trends and issues in the cultural industry. Students will also practice strong critical thinking skills by completing two mini-projects projects aimed at generating innovative ideas for cultural businesses. The students will be able to comprehend the connections between culture, technologies, and our lifestyles, especially in the 4th industrial revolution era. The students will learn thoroughly about "Open Innovation Culture (= Amateur Culture = Democratization of Innovation)," which greatly impacted various cultural domains, such as digital media, industrial design, the food industry, marketing, etc. The students will learn about "Digital-Physical Conve

CDM2007HISTORY OF MODERN AND CONTEMPORARY DESIGNCDM유지
강의개요

HISTORY OF MODERN AND CONTEMPORARY The course explores the evolution of design in order to build up the comprehensive reference for future practice in the related field. It will follow the changes of time in cultural, social, political, economic and technical terms at large and discover how those changes influenced the movements and styles in detail that eventually changed everyday life. The course will be led to an open conclusion of defining the ` contemporary' that we are living in now, on the foundation of the historical understanding of design. The course will provide series of lectures and following discussions. Lectures will offer a chronological overview on history of modern and contemporary design through the movements, styles, key designers and objects. In the following discussions, the innovations, methodologies and definitions that are conceived by design in stages will be debated, followed by student's presentations of their in-depth researches on some selected designers. *Midterm exam will be replaced by individual assignment. *Final exam will be replaced by individual submission. CTM3011DIGITAL BUSINESS STRATEGYCTM유지
강의개요

DIGITAL BUSINESS STRATEGY - CTM3011-01 This is an advanced undergraduate course on the digital economy and the digital business strategy. Three main goals are (1) to understand how people and companies interact in the digital markets, (2) to understand how digital markets should be designed and regulated and (3) to understand how managers can formulate and execute business strategies by leveraging digital resources to create differential value. The course uses a combination of theoretical modeling and empirical evidence in order to achieve these goals. We analyze some key features that are prevalent in digital markets, including network effects, two-sided markets, search and matching, reputation systems and the use of data. We also look into individual markets such as search engines, e-commerce platforms, and media. To understand how people and companies interact in the digital economy. We study how digital technology changes economic activities. We look into the reduction in five distinct economic costs associated with digital economic activity: search costs, replication costs, transportation costs, tracking costs, and verification costs. We also learn about the digital economy eco-system and digital market To study the scope and extent of digital business strategy. We learn about organizational strategy formulated and executed by leveraging digital resources to create differe

CTM3013ECONOMICS OF TECHNOLOGICAL INNOVATIONCTM유지
강의개요

This course is designed to provide a working knowledge of economic principles and real world practices on a range of topics pertaining to technology and innovation. After the brief overview of fundamentals of economics, we will cover various topics including (1) dynamic process of innovation and corporate strategy such as disruptive innovation, vertical integration vs. modularization, learning curve, and determinants of R&D intensity; (2) success and failure of innovative activities; (3) utilization issues of innovation output including first-mover advantage, battles for winner-take-all, patents and standards. The course introduces students to basic economic principles and theories on a range of topics relevant to technology and innovation. The course helps students learn how to apply relevant concepts and frameworks in practice through real-world case studies. Technovation: Technology and Innovation Management PBL CBL, Flipped Classroom , This class is designated as a Social Innovation Certificate (SIC) course. The course contents and practices will be related to social innovation and solving social problems. The Institute of Higher Education Innovation (IHEI) may collect student assignments and course contents for further purpose. MUSIC INFORMATION RETRIEVAL - CTM3022-01 Music information retrieval (MIR) is an emerging field of research that aims to provide intelligent solutions for music listening, performance and other musical activities. This course will introduce various topics in MIR research, and explores how different types of music information can be applied to music discovery, music analysis, interactive performance, visualization, and more. In particular, we will focus on music analysis applying the approach of natural language processing .The goal of this class is to overview the topics and tasks in the field of MIR, and to conduct their own academic research. Introduction to MIR Topics: The course aims to provide an overview of various topics in MIR research. Students will be introduced to the fundamental concepts, techniques, and methodologies employed in the field. This includes understanding the different types of music information, such as audio, symbolic, and textual data, and how they can be extracted and analyzed using computational approaches. The course emphasizes the practical application of music information in various domains. Students will learn how MIR techniques can be utilized for music analysis and visualization. Academic Research: The course aims to develop students' skills and knowledge to independently conduct academic research in MIR. They will explore existing literature

CTM3024INTERNATIONAL MARKETINGCTM개편
강의개요

INTERNATIONAL MARKETING - CTM3024-01 The course aims to familiarize students with essential marketing concepts and practices in the global business environment. Additionally, it aims to provide students with the basic knowledge, techniques, and practical skills necessary to analyze the global marketing environment, formulate and execute an international marketing strategy, and coordinate marketing programs in the international marketplace. A particular emphasis will be placed on the concepts of standardization versus adaptation in the context of global marketing strategies. Upon completion of this course, students will be able to: 1. Evaluate the international marketing environment, specifically examining how global market dynamics and trends influence the selection of country markets and the creation of global marketing campaigns. 2. Compare and contrast various foreign market entry strategies. 3. Utilize marketing concepts to develop global marketing strategies and critically assess key factors for their successful implementation. Topics Contact hours 1 International Marketing Environment 12 2 Drivers for Globalization 3 3 Foreign Market Entry Strategies 6 4 Global Marketing Strategies 20 5 Implementation and Control of Global Marketing Operations 2 Teaching and learning strategies Lectures, tutorials, group presentations, and multimedia materials are the main means employed
